title: Income Eligibility Criterion for Rental Housing
what_it_is: Income Eligibility Criterion for Rental Housing

sections.label: HDB rental flat income flexibility
sections.summary: HDB exercises flexibility so families not meeting eligibility criteria, including bigger families over the income ceiling, can still get a rental flat if they have no other housing options or family support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Whether the criteria are based on household income or per capita income, there will always be a few deserving cases that do not meet the cut-off.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why HDB already exercises flexibility so that families which do not meet the eligibility criteria can still get a rental flat, if they have no other housing options or family support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This includes bigger families, even if their household income exceeds the income ceiling.

sections.label: Rental flat appeals and supply
sections.summary: Applicants rejected on income basis can appeal through their MP or HDB directly, and more rental flats are being stepped up and coming into the market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And while there is shortage now, in future, we should project based on those numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, anyone who has an application for a rental flat and their application is rejected on an income basis can freely put up an appeal, either through their Member of Parliament or to HDB directly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On the supply of rental flats, that is, indeed, being stepped up and there are more rental flats coming into the market.
